hints: Sorting puts equal values next to each other.
Count the first value, then add one whenever the value differs from the preceding sorted value.
An input with one item has one distinct value.
analogy: Sort the numbers into piles; each new pile is a new distinct value.
example: For 2,3,2,2,3, sorting gives 2,2,2,3,3, which has two runs and thus two distinct values.
algorithm: Sort the array and count adjacent changes, starting the count at one.
correctness: Each distinct value forms exactly one contiguous block after sorting, so the number of blocks is the distinct count.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space if sorting copies the input.
